title: Great Oxidation interval
titleZh: 大氧化阶段
summary: Atmospheric and oceanic oxygen rose in a prolonged transformation that changed planetary chemistry and the selective environment for life.

evidenceItems.statement: Mass-independent sulfur isotope signal disappears
Oxidized continental deposits become widespread
Carbon and sulfur cycles reorganize
U–Pb baddeleyite ages bracket the onset at about 2,460–2,426 Ma

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Results; Table 1; SI Tables S1 and S4–S5

uncertaintyItems.statement: Oxygenation was episodic rather than a single instant
Local oceans followed different redox histories

title: Ediacaran macroscopic ecosystems
titleZh: 埃迪卡拉宏体生态系统
summary: Large, complex organisms became conspicuous in late Neoproterozoic seas before the Cambrian diversification of skeletonized animals.

evidenceItems.statement: Body and trace fossils
Repeated assemblages on multiple continents
Stratigraphic association with late Ediacaran environments
CA–ID–TIMS zircon ages place Avalon fossils above the Gaskiers glaciation by about 571 Ma

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Geologic setting; U–Pb geochronology; GSA Data Repository

uncertaintyItems.statement: Biological affinities of many forms remain disputed
Preservational windows strongly structure the record

title: Cambrian radiation
titleZh: 寒武纪大辐射
summary: Animal body plans, ecological interactions and mineralized skeletons expanded rapidly in the early Cambrian fossil record.

evidenceItems.statement: Burgess Shale-type preservation
Small shelly fossils
Trace-fossil diversification

uncertaintyItems.statement: Molecular divergences often predate obvious body fossils
The apparent tempo depends on sampling and preservation

title: Great Ordovician Biodiversification
titleZh: 奥陶纪生物多样化
summary: Marine taxonomic and ecological diversity increased across many groups, building more complex Paleozoic ecosystems.

evidenceItems.statement: Rising genus and family richness
Expansion of reef and tiering structures
Broad geographic recurrence

uncertaintyItems.statement: Regional pulses are asynchronous
Observed richness is sensitive to rock and collection availability

title: Modelled crown-Embryophyta divergence
titleZh: 胚胎植物冠群的模型分化时间
summary: A fossil-calibrated molecular clock estimates a middle Cambrian–Early Ordovician origin for crown land plants; it does not directly date fossil first appearances or terrestrial ecosystem expansion.

evidenceItems.statement: Bayesian relaxed molecular clock using 37 fossil calibrations
Middle Cambrian–Early Ordovician crown-Embryophyta estimate

uncertaintyItems.statement: Divergence estimates are sensitive to clock models and fossil-calibration strategy
Modelled crown divergence is not a direct fossil first appearance or an ecosystem-expansion date

title: Mosaic fin-to-limb and terrestrialization synthesis
titleZh: 鳍—肢与陆地化的镶嵌式综合
summary: A literature synthesis separates the origin of digit-bearing limbs, locomotor changes and full terrestriality rather than presenting one fish-to-land step or a chain of direct ancestors.

evidenceItems.statement: Fins, girdles, digits and joint mobility changed in different combinations across Devonian and Early Carboniferous forms
The synthesis treats digit-bearing limbs, walking and full terrestriality as distinguishable evolutionary questions

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Abstract; What Can We Learn from This Information?; Conclusions

uncertaintyItems.statement: This broad 385–350 Ma display is an editorial synthesis window, not a single dated event or a taxon range
Possession of digits does not by itself establish terrestrial ecology, a modern walking gait or direct ancestry

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Our Cast of Characters; What Can We Learn from This Information?

title: Eifelian Zachełmie digit trackways
titleZh: 艾菲尔期 Zachełmie 具趾足迹
regions: Zachełmie Quarry, Holy Cross Mountains, Poland
summary: Trackways and isolated prints preserve digit impressions from an Eifelian surface, providing trace-fossil evidence for a limbed trackmaker without naming the animal that made them.

evidenceItems.statement: Quadrupedal trackways, isolated footprints and digit impressions occur on securely dated early Middle Devonian bedding surfaces

uncertaintyItems.statement: A footprint records a trace-making appendage and gait, not the trackmaker's body taxonomy, complete anatomy or ancestor–descendant identity
The displayed 393.47–387.95 Ma interval is the atlas's current Eifelian stage window, not an analytical error bar on one footprint

title: Tiktaalik body-plan mosaic
titleZh: Tiktaalik 身体结构镶嵌
regions: Fram Formation, southern Ellesmere Island, Nunavut, Canada
summary: The holotype and referred material combine scales, fin rays and fish-like jaws with a mobile neck, modified ear region, robust ribs and a functional wrist joint.

evidenceItems.statement: NUFV 108 and referred material preserve a shortened skull roof, mobile neck, modified ear region, robust overlapping ribs and fin-bearing paired appendages

uncertaintyItems.statement: The anatomical mosaic and depositional setting support hypotheses about shallow marginal habitats but do not show that Tiktaalik routinely walked on land

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Abstract; discussion of palaeoenvironment and functional interpretation

uncertaintyItems.statement: A phylogenetically intermediate combination does not identify Tiktaalik as a direct ancestor of later tetrapods

title: Tiktaalik pectoral fin and mobile wrist
titleZh: Tiktaalik 胸鳍与可动腕部
regions: Fram Formation, southern Ellesmere Island, Nunavut, Canada
summary: The pectoral fin retains fin rays while its endoskeleton includes a mobile, load-transmitting wrist-like joint and distal elements arranged within the fin.

evidenceItems.statement: The pectoral-fin endoskeleton includes a robust humerus, radius and ulna, wrist-like joints and distal radials while retaining lepidotrichial fin rays

uncertaintyItems.statement: Load transmission inferred from joint geometry is a functional interpretation; the appendage remains a fin and does not preserve free digits or a witnessed gait

title: Elpistostege digit-bearing fin endoskeleton
titleZh: Elpistostege 具指样内骨骼的鳍
summary: Computed tomography of one articulated specimen reveals four proximodistal radial rows and two distal rows interpreted as digits or putative digits inside a pectoral fin that still bears fin rays.

evidenceItems.statement: Specimen MHNM 06-2067 preserves a 1.57-metre articulated body and a CT-resolved pectoral-fin skeleton with branched carpals and distal digit-like rows

uncertaintyItems.statement: Digit homology and the potential sister position to other tetrapods are analytical interpretations, and the appendage remains a fin with lepidotrichia

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Abstract; comparative anatomy and phylogenetic analyses

uncertaintyItems.statement: The displayed 382.31–372.15 Ma interval is the current Frasnian stage window for the formation context, not a direct radiometric date on MHNM 06-2067

title: Acanthostega eight-digit forelimb
titleZh: Acanthostega 八趾前肢
summary: New limb material showed eight digits in the Acanthostega forelimb, rejecting a fixed five-digit primitive condition and supporting an aquatic context for early digit-bearing limbs.

evidenceItems.statement: The described Acanthostega forelimb has eight digits; the same study reports seven in the Ichthyostega hindlimb and six in Tulerpeton

uncertaintyItems.statement: Eight digits diagnose the described limb material; they neither define a universal ancestral digit count nor demonstrate terrestrial walking

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Abstract; discussion of polydactyly and aquatic adaptation

uncertaintyItems.statement: The displayed 372.15–358.86 Ma interval is the current Famennian stage window, not a direct numerical date on each limb specimen

title: Ichthyostega three-dimensional joint mobility
titleZh: Ichthyostega 三维关节活动度重建
summary: A three-dimensional reconstruction and comparative joint analysis found that Ichthyostega lacked the limb rotations required for a typical lateral-sequence walk.

evidenceItems.statement: Micro-CT-based reconstruction quantified shoulder and hip ranges of motion against five living tetrapod analogues

uncertaintyItems.statement: The result may represent an early restricted-mobility stage or a specialization unique to Ichthyostega; it is not a gait model for every early tetrapod
Joint range constrains feasible motions but does not directly observe behaviour, substrate use or every movement available to the living animal

title: Amniote diversification
titleZh: 羊膜动物分化
summary: Early amniotes split into the major lineages that would later produce mammals and reptiles, including birds.

evidenceItems.statement: Diagnostic skull openings
Reproductive and skeletal adaptations inferred from phylogeny
Carboniferous body fossils

uncertaintyItems.statement: The earliest members are rare
Exact divergence dates depend on tree calibration

title: End-Permian mass extinction
titleZh: 二叠纪末大灭绝
summary: The most severe known Phanerozoic biotic crisis reorganized marine and terrestrial ecosystems near the Permian–Triassic boundary.

evidenceItems.statement: Abrupt fossil range terminations
Carbon-isotope excursion
Volcanic and warming proxies
Dated Meishan ash beds bound the main extinction interval to about 60 ± 48 kyr

uncertaintyItems.statement: Kill mechanisms interacted across ocean and land
Regional ecological collapse and recovery were asynchronous

title: Triassic ecological recovery
titleZh: 三叠纪生态恢复
summary: Ecosystems rebuilt in multiple pulses after the end-Permian crisis, eventually supporting new marine and terrestrial radiations.

evidenceItems.statement: Changing food-web structure
New reptile radiations
Recovery of reef and pelagic systems

uncertaintyItems.statement: Recovery duration differs by metric and region
Repeated Early Triassic environmental stress delayed some communities

title: Early angiosperm crown-lineage diversification estimates
titleZh: 被子植物主要冠群的早期分化估计
summary: A metacalibrated time-tree estimates Early Cretaceous diversification of major flowering-plant crown lineages; it is not direct evidence of fossil first appearances or ecological dominance.

evidenceItems.statement: Metacalibrated crown-lineage estimates from 137 fossil calibrations

uncertaintyItems.statement: Estimated ages depend on fossil calibrations and molecular-clock models

title: K–Pg mass extinction
titleZh: 白垩纪—古近纪灭绝
summary: An impact-driven global crisis ended the non-avian dinosaurs and many marine groups while opening ecological space for surviving lineages.

evidenceItems.statement: Iridium-rich boundary layer
Chicxulub crater
Abrupt fossil turnover
High-precision 40Ar/39Ar ages resolve impact and boundary extinction as synchronous within about 32 kyr

uncertaintyItems.statement: Deccan volcanism contributed background environmental stress
Survival and recovery patterns varied among regions and clades

title: Paleocene–Eocene Thermal Maximum
titleZh: 古新世—始新世极热事件
summary: A geologically rapid carbon release and warming interval coincided with major migrations, body-size shifts and marine turnover.

evidenceItems.statement: Negative carbon-isotope excursion
Deep-sea benthic extinction
Poleward biogeographic shifts

uncertaintyItems.statement: Carbon sources and release pacing remain debated
Onset and recovery durations depend on archive resolution

title: Early Eocene perissodactyl radiation and dispersal
titleZh: 早始新世奇蹄目辐射与扩散
summary: Odd-toed ungulates appeared and rapidly diversified into many of the dominant large-herbivore roles of Eocene northern continents.

evidenceItems.statement: Rapid early Eocene occurrence expansion
Diverse dental and locomotor morphologies
Intercontinental first appearances

uncertaintyItems.statement: The precise ancestral group and relationships of early branches remain debated
First appearances reflect sampling as well as evolution

title: Eocene–Oligocene transition
titleZh: 始新世—渐新世转型
summary: Global cooling, Antarctic glaciation and habitat reorganization coincided with major mammalian and marine faunal turnover.

evidenceItems.statement: Marine oxygen-isotope shift
Antarctic ice-volume proxies
European Grande Coupure turnover

uncertaintyItems.statement: Immigration, climate and habitat change contributed differently by region
Ecological replacement was not a simple one-to-one competition

title: Late Miocene C4-vegetation expansion
titleZh: 晚中新世 C4 植被扩张
summary: Fossil tooth-enamel isotopes record a widespread, regionally asynchronous increase in C4-plant biomass; they do not alone demonstrate open grassland or faunal adaptation.

evidenceItems.statement: Fossil tooth-enamel δ13C records from four continents

uncertaintyItems.statement: The increase occurred earlier at lower latitudes and was not globally synchronous
Isotope-inferred C4 biomass is not equivalent to open-grassland dominance
Tooth-enamel δ13C is an animal-diet and local-habitat proxy; it cannot identify which C4 plant lineages supplied the biomass or assume diet is proportional to vegetation cover

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Methods and interpretation of enamel carbon isotopes

title: Quaternary megafaunal extinctions
titleZh: 第四纪巨型动物灭绝
summary: Large-bodied vertebrates disappeared in geographically staggered waves during the late Quaternary.

evidenceItems.statement: Radiometric last-appearance records
Archaeological association
Paleoenvironmental archives

uncertaintyItems.statement: Relative effects of human pressure and climate vary by continent
Last-appearance dates underestimate true extinction when sampling is sparse

title: Dapingian cryptospore assemblage
titleZh: 大坪期隐孢子组合
summary: Five cryptospore genera from a source-dated 473–471 Ma Argentine assemblage provide early evidence of plants on emerged land without identifying a bryophyte crown group.

evidenceItems.statement: Naked and envelope-enclosed monads and tetrads from one biostratigraphically controlled horizon

uncertaintyItems.statement: Cryptospores do not identify a crown bryophyte lineage or the exact place and time of embryophyte origin

title: Late Ordovician spore-mass fragments
titleZh: 晚奥陶世含孢子团植物碎片
clades: Early land plants; liverwort affinity tentative
summary: Caradoc-age fragments from an Oman core preserve dense cryptospore masses and probable sporangial covering, directly linking early spores to land plants while leaving crown affinity unresolved.

evidenceItems.statement: Twelve fragments contain permanent tetrads or dyads, and some retain presumed sporangial covering

uncertaintyItems.statement: Caradoc is a legacy regional unit, so the Sandbian–Katian display window is deliberately broad
Lamellate spore walls suggest liverwort affinity, but missing elaters and unresolved early-land-plant topology prevent a crown assignment

title: Asteroxylon rooting-system reconstruction
titleZh: 星木属根系三维重建
summary: Evidence-based 3D reconstructions separate three axis types in Asteroxylon mackiei and show an extinct anisotomous route to rooting axes without projecting that anatomy onto all lycophytes.

evidenceItems.statement: Independent serial-section and peel reconstructions recover leafy shoot, root-bearing and rooting axes

uncertaintyItems.statement: The reconstructed developmental mechanism belongs to Asteroxylon and is not asserted for all Lycophyta

title: Givetian Metzgeriothallus body fossils
titleZh: 吉维特期 Metzgeriothallus 植物体化石
regions: Catskill Delta succession, eastern New York
summary: Givetian shale and siltstone lenses preserve thalloid Metzgeriothallus sharonae gametophytes and an associated sporophyte capsule, a liverwort body-fossil record rather than a crown-origin date.

evidenceItems.statement: Polarized-light study reveals bifurcating thalli with a medial costa and an associated sporophyte capsule

uncertaintyItems.statement: A Givetian occurrence cannot date crown Marchantiophyta or prove absence from older rocks
The fossil morphology is not generalized to all living or extinct liverwort lineages

title: Extant gymnosperm phylogenomic backbone
titleZh: 现生裸子植物系统基因组骨架
summary: A nuclear phylogenomic analysis spanning all living gymnosperm families recovered a Gnepine topology and a cycads-plus-Ginkgo branch while leaving fossils and chronological ranges outside the claim.

evidenceItems.statement: All 13 living gymnosperm families sampled across up to 1,308 nuclear loci

uncertaintyItems.statement: Gene-tree conflict and alternative subset results keep the Gnepine placement a published hypothesis rather than permanent consensus
The topology concerns sampled living lineages and supplies neither fossil ranges nor an extinct-seed-plant tree

title: 2011 model of living-cycad radiation
titleZh: 2011 年现生苏铁辐射模型
summary: A 2011 fossil-calibrated model placed most sampled living cycad species within the last roughly 12 million years; later fossil-integrated studies require a less synchronous and more deeply rooted interpretation.

evidenceItems.statement: Fossil-calibrated timetrees of sampled living cycad species and genera

uncertaintyItems.statement: Later fossil, tectonic and total-evidence treatments recover older deep nodes and weaken a simple globally synchronous radiation
The 12 Ma window concerns sampled living radiations, not Cycadales origin or fossil first appearance

title: Modelled crown age of extant Cycadaceae
titleZh: 现生苏铁科冠群模型年龄
regions: Global Cycas plastome sample with Palawan calibration
summary: A combined plastome, fossil and tectonic calibration scheme yielded mean crown-age estimates of 69.31 and 42.88 Ma under different tree priors, without converting either model result into a fossil range.

evidenceItems.statement: Whole-plastome phylogeny evaluated under alternative fossil, tectonic and tree-prior schemes

uncertaintyItems.statement: Calibration scheme and tree prior substantially change the estimate, with underconstrained alternatives spanning much wider ages
The result concerns the crown of living Cycadaceae, not all Cycadales and not a directly observed fossil first appearance

title: Modelled contraction of cycad latitudinal range
titleZh: 苏铁纬度分布收缩模型
summary: A total-evidence biogeographic model inferred broad Cretaceous–Palaeogene latitudes followed by contraction toward the present tropical–subtropical distribution, while exposing how strongly fossils change extinction estimates.

evidenceItems.statement: 321 living species, 60 fossil leaf species and time-stratified process-based biogeography

uncertaintyItems.statement: The broad 66–11.63 Ma display window summarizes a modelled transition and is not one dated extinction pulse
Fossil omissions, uncertain placements and model assumptions can alter dates, ancestral areas and inferred local extirpation counts

title: Tiaojishan Ginkgo-like fossil wood
titleZh: 天义山组银杏样化石木材
summary: One anatomically diagnosed fossil wood from the Middle–Late Jurassic transition records a Ginkgo-like xylem combination while remaining an isolated organ taxon rather than a whole plant or phylum first appearance.

evidenceItems.statement: Specimen PB22285, Tiaojishan stratigraphy and wood anatomy illustrated in transverse, tangential and radial section

uncertaintyItems.statement: The isolated wood cannot be safely linked to any particular co-occurring Ginkgo foliage species
A 153–165 Ma specimen does not establish the first appearance of Ginkgophyta or continuous survival of Ginkgo biloba from the Jurassic

title: Modelled hemispheric pattern in extant conifer nodes
titleZh: 现生针叶树节点的半球模型格局
regions: Northern and Southern Hemisphere living-species sample
summary: A 489-species time tree found older combined median node ages in predominantly Southern Hemisphere conifer lineages than in sampled Northern Hemisphere lineages, a relative living-lineage pattern rather than a fossil range.

evidenceItems.statement: 489 living conifer species and 16 fossil calibrations yield combined medians of 8.7 versus 5.2 Ma

uncertaintyItems.statement: The displayed endpoints are comparative median node ages, not the duration of one radiation event or the origin of Araucariaceae
Absolute ages may be biased young, Gnetales were excluded and the proposed climate mechanism remains interpretive

title: Calibration-sensitive crown-angiosperm timescale
titleZh: 校准敏感的被子植物冠群年代模型
summary: A fossil-integrated molecular-clock study preferred a tightly constrained Late Jurassic crown estimate, while alternative treatments of the same calibration densities produced much older intervals.

evidenceItems.statement: 25,685 fossil occurrences informed 110 calibrations on a 644-species, 83-gene phylogeny

uncertaintyItems.statement: The displayed 152.99–151.46 Ma interval is the authors' preferred hard-bound strategy; soft-bound and skew-T strategies yielded 172.53–158.45 Ma and 261.26–212.30 Ma
The result is a calibration-dependent crown model, not a directly observed Jurassic flower or fossil first appearance

title: Barremian Montsechia in freshwater habitats
titleZh: 巴列姆期淡水生境中的 Montsechia
regions: El Montsec and Las Hoyas, Spain
summary: More than one thousand specimens preserve leafy axes and closed single-seeded fruits consistent with a submerged freshwater angiosperm, without fixing crown placement or flowering-plant ancestry.

evidenceItems.statement: More than 1,000 specimens with flexible axes, thin cuticles, rare stomata and closed single-seeded fruits

uncertaintyItems.statement: A morphology-based position near Ceratophyllum is a hypothesis and does not show that the angiosperm ancestor was aquatic
Current Barremian boundaries are used for display; the paper reported the deposits as approximately 130–125 Ma

title: Cratolirion whole-plant monocot
titleZh: Cratolirion 单子叶植物整株化石
summary: An anatomically preserved plant from roots to reproductive organs supports a crown-monocot assignment at about 115 Ma, but not a monocot origin date or a modern-family identification.

evidenceItems.statement: Root system, narrow parallel-veined leaves, vascular anatomy and trimerous reproductive organs preserved in one plant

uncertaintyItems.statement: Cratolirion is a fossil crown monocot, not proof of the first monocot or an assignment to a living lily family

title: Early Cretaceous Leefructus eudicot
titleZh: 义县组早期真双子叶植物 Leefructus
regions: Lower Yixian Formation, western Liaoning, China
summary: A whole-plant fossil preserves deeply trilobate leaves and a reproductive axis with five partly united carpels, supporting an Early Cretaceous eudicot assignment while leaving family affinity provisional.

evidenceItems.statement: Holotype and reconstruction link diagnostic leaves to an axillary reproductive axis with five long, narrow carpels

uncertaintyItems.statement: Ranunculaceae affinity was suggested from morphology; it is not an uncontested family assignment or the global first appearance of eudicots

title: Great Plains C3–C4 phytolith transition
titleZh: 北美大平原 C3–C4 植硅体转变
regions: Central Great Plains, Nebraska and Kansas, United States
summary: Fourteen well-preserved palaeosol phytolith assemblages record a regional rise of chloridoid and other potentially C4 grasses within heterogeneous mixed C3–C4 habitats.

evidenceItems.statement: By about 5.5 Ma, chloridoid and other potentially C4 PACMAD grass short cells reached roughly 50–60% of the grass component

uncertaintyItems.statement: The 50–60% estimate is within the grass component, not total vegetation, and PACMAD-type morphologies are not all diagnostic of C4 photosynthesis
Fourteen selected assemblages from the central Great Plains do not establish a synchronous continental or global transition

title: Qianodus tooth whorls in the late Aeronian
titleZh: 晚埃隆期黔齿鱼牙旋
summary: Twenty-three isolated tooth whorls, including holotype IVPP V26641, provide approximately 439 Ma direct evidence of jawed-vertebrate dentition while remaining disarticulated stem-chondrichthyan material rather than a crown-shark body or a global first-appearance datum.

evidenceItems.statement: Holotype IVPP V26641 and referred tooth whorls preserve non-shedding teeth added lingually in offset rows

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Systematic palaeontology; tooth-whorl development and histology

evidenceItems.statement: The Rongxi Formation occurrence lies in the Ozarkodina guizhouensis conodont biozone, late Aeronian, at approximately 439 Ma

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Supplementary Information: Geological setting and biostratigraphy

uncertaintyItems.statement: No articulated body or jaw is known, and co-occurring scales and spines cannot be assigned to or excluded from Qianodus
The specimen-level occurrence supports early direct gnathostome dental evidence, not the origin or global FAD of jaws, Chondrichthyes or crown sharks

title: Fanjingshania dermoskeleton and shoulder remodelling
titleZh: 梵净山鱼皮骨骼与肩带重塑
summary: Holotype IVPP V27433.1 and more than one thousand isolated elements document a roughly 439 Ma stem-chondrichthyan dermoskeleton; later tomography of six referred shoulder elements shows cyclical bone-and-dentine resorption without supplying an articulated body or associated teeth.

evidenceItems.statement: Holotype IVPP V27433.1 is a pinnal shoulder plate portion fused to a pectoral fin-spine fragment, with more than one thousand isolated referred elements

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Systematic palaeontology: Holotype, referred material, locality and horizon

evidenceItems.statement: Specimens IVPP V27433.8–12 and V27434.2 reveal five growth centres and cyclical resorption and remodelling of bone and dentine in the spine–plate complex

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Results: structure and development; Discussion: dermal skeletal remodelling

uncertaintyItems.statement: The material is disarticulated and no assignable dentition is known, so the full-body reconstruction remains comparative rather than specimen-complete
Fanjingshania is treated as a stem chondrichthyan and cannot be synonymized with Qianodus or presented as a crown shark from co-occurrence alone

title: Articulated Xiushanosteus from the Chongqing Lagerstätte
titleZh: 重庆特异埋藏群的秀山鱼关节躯体
regions: Huixingshao Formation, Yongdong, Xiushan, Chongqing, China
summary: Holotype IVPP V300001 and twenty referred specimens preserve an approximately 30 mm, near-complete placoderm-grade stem gnathostome at about 436 Ma, directly exposing a mosaic skull roof and body plan without identifying an ancestor of crown jawed vertebrates.

evidenceItems.statement: Holotype IVPP V300001 and referred specimens IVPP V300002–V300021 preserve articulated or near-complete bodies from the middle-to-late Telychian Huixingshao Formation

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Systematic palaeontology: material, locality and horizon

evidenceItems.statement: The skull roof combines character states otherwise distributed among major placoderm grades and approaches the osteichthyan pattern in the arrangement of paired bones

uncertaintyItems.statement: Placoderms form an evolutionary grade in the study and early stem-gnathostome relationships remain weakly resolved, so Xiushanosteus is not presented as a direct ancestor
Its abundance within one Lagerstätte is not evidence of global ecological dominance or a global FAD for placoderms or jawed vertebrates

title: Shenacanthus combines chondrichthyan and armoured traits
titleZh: 申氏棘鱼兼具软骨鱼与甲胄特征
regions: Huixingshao Formation, Yongdong, Xiushan, Chongqing, China
summary: The sole near-complete holotype IVPP V300000 records a roughly 436 Ma total-group chondrichthyan body with minute scales and a chondrichthyan-like branchial region but unexpectedly large thoracic armour plates; the exact stem position remains analysis-sensitive.

evidenceItems.statement: Holotype IVPP V300000 preserves a near-complete body with minute scales, no facial dermal bones, a chondrichthyan-like posterior branchial region and macromeric thoracic armour

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Systematic palaeontology and description of Shenacanthus

uncertaintyItems.statement: Only one specimen is known and no teeth are preserved; maximum-parsimony and Bayesian analyses differ in the details of its position within the chondrichthyan total group
The mosaic body plan is not a crown-shark diagnosis and does not establish the global first appearance of Chondrichthyes

title: Gladbachus reveals a mosaic stem-chondrichthyan anatomy
titleZh: 格拉德巴赫鱼揭示软骨鱼干群镶嵌解剖
regions: Lower Plattenkalk, Unterthal, Bergisch Gladbach, Germany
summary: CT and histology of the single compressed specimen UMZC 2000.32 reveal a roughly 385 Ma stem chondrichthyan combining placoderm-like, osteichthyan-like and chondrichthyan features, demonstrating disparity without supplying a crown-shark ancestor.

evidenceItems.statement: UMZC 2000.32 preserves portions of the neurocranium, jaws, hyoid and gill arches, pectoral girdle, cartilage, scales and teeth in the Upper Givetian Lower Plattenkalk

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Material and methods: Specimens; Results: specimen description

evidenceItems.statement: The study's phylogenetic analysis recovers Gladbachus on the chondrichthyan stem despite its anatomically incongruent character combination

uncertaintyItems.statement: The caudal region is missing and the fossil is dorsoventrally compressed, so total body length and suspension-feeding ecology are reconstructions rather than direct observations

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Specimen condition; anatomical reconstruction; Discussion of feeding

uncertaintyItems.statement: The event documents one stem chondrichthyan and cannot date the crown group, a shark-like body-plan origin or a global first appearance

title: Priscomyzon preserves a Devonian lamprey oral disc
titleZh: 古圆口鱼保存泥盆纪七鳃鳗口盘
regions: Waterloo Farm, Witpoort Formation, Eastern Cape, South Africa
summary: The 4.2 cm holotype AM5750 from Famennian strata preserves a large oral disc, fourteen circumoral teeth and a branchial basket, establishing a specimen-level total-group lamprey record without demonstrating a modern lifecycle or crown-group FAD.

evidenceItems.statement: Holotype AM5750 preserves a large oral disc with fourteen circumoral teeth and a well-defined branchial basket in a 4.2 cm body
The specimen comes from the Famennian Witpoort Formation at Waterloo Farm, approximately 360 Ma on the source's numerical framing

uncertaintyItems.statement: A single fossil does not preserve an ammocoete stage, metamorphosis, parasitism or migration and therefore cannot establish a modern lamprey lifecycle
The occurrence is treated as total-group lamprey evidence, not a directly dated crown-Petromyzontida origin or global FAD

title: Myxinikela records a Carboniferous stem hagfish
titleZh: 马松溪似盲鳗记录石炭纪盲鳗干群
regions: Francis Creek Shale, former Pit 11, Illinois, United States
summary: Holotype FMNH PF15373 and paratype FMNH PF8472 from Moscovian Francis Creek Shale preserve a cyclostome–hagfish mosaic at roughly 310–307 Ma; the revised material is stem-hagfish evidence and is excluded from the crown-Myxini range.

evidenceItems.statement: Holotype FMNH PF15373 and paratype FMNH PF8472 preserve a body outline and soft-tissue traces combining general cyclostome characters with hagfish specializations
The specimens measure 73.3 and 62.5 mm and come from the Moscovian Francis Creek Shale at the former Pit 11 locality

uncertaintyItems.statement: The two specimens preserve differently and the paratype does not contain definitive cartilage, so several anatomical identifications remain equivocal
Myxinikela is a stem or putative total-group hagfish, not a crown Myxini datum; the fossils do not establish deep-sea habitat, slime production or crown-hagfish timing

title: Eifelian Cheirolepis endoskeleton
titleZh: 艾菲尔期 Cheirolepis 内骨骼
regions: Achanarras Limestone, Tynet Burn and Gamrie, Scotland
summary: CT examination of named museum specimens reveals a mosaic of neurocranial, suspensorial, pectoral-fin and scale characters in an early ray-finned fish.

evidenceItems.statement: NMS.1877.30.5/NHMUK P.62908 preserves the braincase, while NMS.1956.19 preserves the hyomandibula and both pectoral endoskeletal girdles; additional parasphenoid material comes from NHMUK P.4051a/b, MCZ 6039, NHMUK P.66863 and NMS.1892.8.60.

The scanned material shows an imperforate propterygium, an imperforate hyomandibular shaft and peg-and-socket scale articulation alongside character states shared with later ray-finned fishes and osteichthyan outgroups.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Neurocranium; Hyomandibula; Pectoral fin endoskeleton; Body scales

uncertaintyItems.statement: The 390.4–388.1 Ma values are the study's numerical translation of a late Eifelian biostratigraphic assignment using the 2012 timescale, not a direct radiometric date on either specimen.
These specimens do not establish the global first appearance of Actinopterygii, a direct ancestor of living ray-finned fishes or absence of an older unsampled lineage.

title: Fukangichthys and crown-actinopterygian recalibration
titleZh: Fukangichthys 与辐鳍鱼冠群重新校准
regions: Kelamayi Formation, Xinjiang, China; comparative CT sample
summary: CT anatomy and phylogenetic analyses placed scanilepiforms on the polypterid stem, moving many Palaeozoic ray-fins outside the living crown and revising fossil calibrations.

evidenceItems.statement: Analyses of Fukangichthys specimens IVPP V4096.6 and IVPP V4096.13, compared with ropefish BMNH 2016.9.22.3, recovered scanilepiforms as stem polypterids and shifted the minimum calibration for crown Actinopterygii about 45 million years younger.

uncertaintyItems.statement: The displayed 247.0–241.464 Ma envelope is the current Anisian stage translation for navigation; it is not a direct date on IVPP V4096.6 or IVPP V4096.13 and does not equal the crown-actinopterygian origin time.

The placement is topology- and character-sampling-sensitive; the 2014 anatomical revision recovered Fukangichthys within Neopterygii, so that earlier result is historical context rather than interchangeable support for the 2017 placement.

title: Genomic support for living Holostei
titleZh: 现生全骨鱼类的基因组支持
regions: Extant comparative genome and transcriptome sample
summary: The spotted gar genome and bowfin transcriptomic evidence support gars plus bowfin as a living clade sister to teleosts and provide a pre-teleost-duplication genomic reference.

evidenceItems.statement: A 25-vertebrate phylogenomic matrix of 243 one-to-one proteins (97,794 aligned amino acids), together with bowfin transcriptome data and conserved synteny, supported Holostei and placed gar divergence before the teleost genome duplication.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Genome assembly and annotation; Gar informs vertebrate genome evolution

uncertaintyItems.statement: This is present-day genomic evidence derived from one 90× spotted-gar assembly plus comparative transcriptomes and genomes, not a fossil date, proof of morphological stasis or a complete sample of living holostean variation.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Genome assembly and annotation; Online Methods

uncertaintyItems.statement: Using gar as an outgroup to the teleost genome duplication does not show that duplication alone caused teleost species richness.

title: Modelled age of teleost genome duplication 3R
titleZh: 真骨鱼 3R 全基因组复制的模型年代
summary: Molecular dating of 30 duplicated-gene pairs places teleost 3R before the study's crown-teleost interval and is compatible with delayed rediploidization.

evidenceItems.statement: Independent-locus and gene-birth models applied to 30 ohnologue pairs yielded a 286.18–267.20 Ma 95% highest-posterior-density interval for 3R; the same study estimated crown Teleostei at 254.36–234.16 Ma.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Results: The age of Ts3R; Discussion

uncertaintyItems.statement: The interval is a molecular-model posterior, not a fossil occurrence or an instantaneous cytological observation; different duplicates can resolve after prolonged rediploidization, rearrangement and gene loss.
The authors found 3R predating their crown-teleost interval by 12.84–52.02 million years and did not treat the duplication as a sufficient deterministic cause of later teleost diversity.

title: Anisian stem-teleosteomorph diversity
titleZh: 安尼期干群真骨鱼总群多样性
summary: Three named small-bodied fishes from a Middle Triassic locality document early stem-teleosteomorph taxonomic, anatomical and ecological disparity.

evidenceItems.statement: Pseudopholidoctenus (holotype MB.f.18641; paratypes MB.f.19904–19906), Barschichthys (holotype MB.f.19907; MB.f.19908–19909) and Ruedersdorfia (holotype MB.f.19910) preserve distinct character combinations at one approximately 244 Ma locality.

uncertaintyItems.statement: The source assigns these fishes to the stem of Teleosteomorpha/Pan-Teleostei; they are not a global fossil first appearance of crown Teleostei.

The current Anisian stage envelope is broader than the paper's approximate 244 Ma locality age; one quarry cannot establish synchronous global radiation, and small adult size alone does not prove developmental miniaturization.

title: Neopterygian caudal-fin developmental mosaic
titleZh: 新鳍鱼尾鳍发育镶嵌
regions: Extant comparative developmental and anatomical sample
summary: Comparative anatomy and developmental series show that gar and teleosts share a hypural-diastema complex while leaving its homology and evolutionary route unresolved.

evidenceItems.statement: Adults and developmental series of stickleback, zebrafish, spotted gar, bowfin, paddlefish and bichir show a gar–teleost hypural-diastema complex and that the earliest caudal lepidotrichia contribute to external fin symmetry.

uncertaintyItems.statement: Presence in gars prevents treating the complete complex as an unconditional teleost synapomorphy; descent with repeated loss, parallel origin and latent homology remain alternative explanations, with the paper favouring latent parallelism.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Discussion: homology by descent and latent homology hypotheses

uncertaintyItems.statement: The complex includes connective tissue and vasculature that fossils seldom preserve, so skeletal gaps alone cannot fully score the living developmental complex.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Definition of the hypural diastema complex; fossil comparison

title: Genome-structure support for Eloposteoglossocephala
titleZh: 基因组结构支持海鲢—骨舌鱼共同支系
summary: Gene trees and independent chromosome-structure markers support Elopomorpha plus Osteoglossomorpha as sister to Clupeocephala among sampled living teleosts.

evidenceItems.statement: Seven new elopomorph genomes plus 18 public genomes were analysed with 955 single-copy gene trees and 3,041 adjacency markers; sequence and chromosome-rearrangement methods converged on Elopomorpha plus Osteoglossomorpha.

uncertaintyItems.statement: The result is a topology for the sampled extant lineages, not a complete species-level teleost tree; the paper found no exclusive unambiguous morphological character for the proposed clade.
The inferred ancestral chromosome fusion is reconstructed from extant genome structure and is not a directly observed ancient event or a fossil first appearance.

title: Kungurian Gerobatrachus stem batrachian
titleZh: Kungur期 Gerobatrachus 干群蛙螈类
regions: Clear Fork Group, Baylor County, Texas, USA
summary: The articulated holotype USNM 489135 records a Permian frog–salamander character mosaic recovered as a stem batrachian.

evidenceItems.statement: USNM 489135 is the sole holotype from USNM locality 40971, Don’s Dump Fish Quarry.

uncertaintyItems.statement: The Kungurian display interval uses the current chart; the source reports Early Permian Leonardian, not a direct radiometric specimen age.

title: Early Triassic Triadobatrachus μCT
titleZh: 早三叠世 Triadobatrachus 微型 CT
regions: Middle Sakamena equivalent beds near Betsiaka, Madagascar
summary: μCT recovers hidden anatomy in the unique holotype and bounds an early frog-lineage body before crown Anura.

evidenceItems.statement: MNHN.F.MAE.126 is the unique part-and-counterpart holotype with caudal vertebrae and fifteen presacrals.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Material; anatomy; trunk evolution; calibration review

uncertaintyItems.statement: The Late Induan–early Olenekian provenance is historical and imprecise; neither crown Anura nor specialized jumping is directly established.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Material; anatomy; trunk evolution; calibration review

title: Norian Funcusvermis stem caecilian
titleZh: 诺利期 Funcusvermis 蚓螈干群
regions: Thunderstorm Ridge, upper Blue Mesa Member, Chinle Formation, Arizona, USA
summary: Isolated named elements from at least 76 individuals place a caecilian total-group record inside a dated Norian bonebed.

evidenceItems.statement: Holotype PEFO 43891 and named paratypes/referred elements include jaws, vertebrae and femora.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Systematic palaeontology; locality and geochronology; phylogeny

uncertaintyItems.statement: The assemblage is not one articulated animal; published analyses place it outside crown Gymnophiona and the locality is not a global FAD.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Systematic palaeontology; locality and geochronology; phylogeny

title: Oxfordian Beiyanerpeton salamandroid
titleZh: 牛津期 Beiyanerpeton 蝾螈总科成员
regions: Tiaojishan Formation, Hengdaozi, western Liaoning, China
summary: Six articulated specimens support an Oxfordian salamandroid record and preserve larval structures interpreted as neoteny.

evidenceItems.statement: PKUP V0601 is the holotype; PKUP V0602–V0606 are referred specimens.

uncertaintyItems.statement: The 157 ± 3 Ma U–Pb date comes from overlying trachyandesite, and both neoteny and placement remain interpretations.

title: Oligocene Ymboirana crown-caecilian candidate
titleZh: 渐新世 Ymboirana 冠群蚓螈候选
regions: Tremembé Formation near Tremembé, São Paulo, Brazil
summary: CT-informed comparative anatomy identifies a partial caecilian skeleton as a provisional member of a living aquatic family.

evidenceItems.statement: DGM 1462-R is the part-and-counterpart holotype preserving skull, mandibles, atlas and 66 trunk vertebrae.

uncertaintyItems.statement: No unambiguous typhlonectid synapomorphy was identified and formal phylogenetic testing remains pending; aquatic behaviour is not preserved.

title: Xenopus tropicalis draft genome
titleZh: 热带爪蟾草图基因组
regions: Laboratory genome dataset; Nigerian inbred line
summary: A named draft assembly provides a living frog genomic reference while retaining its one-individual and draft-assembly boundary.

evidenceItems.statement: A seventh-generation inbred female yielded about 7.6-fold shotgun coverage, 1.51 Gbp of scaffolds and assembly accession AAMC00000000.

uncertaintyItems.statement: The genome is not a direct record of amphibian ancestors, divergence time, every amphibian genome or universal phenotype.

title: Xenopus thyroid-receptor metamorphosis experiment
titleZh: 爪蟾甲状腺激素受体变态实验
summary: Receptor-knockout tadpoles experimentally separate TRα and TRβ roles across hindlimb and tail metamorphosis.

evidenceItems.statement: TRβ knockouts retained healthy notochord five days after stage 62 and showed reduced matrix-degrading expression; TRα knockouts developed hindlimbs precociously.

uncertaintyItems.statement: Effects differ by receptor and organ and cannot be generalized to every amphibian species, tissue or evolutionary origin.

title: Extant 7,238-species amphibian timetree
titleZh: 现生 7,238 种两栖动物时间树
summary: A 10,000-tree posterior represents 7,238 extant species while exposing which placements have molecular data and which use taxonomy.

evidenceItems.statement: The 15-gene matrix contains 4,061 amphibian species; remaining species were softly placed within taxonomic constraints.

uncertaintyItems.statement: Model nodes are not fossils or observed origins, and the 2014 taxonomy does not replace current COL26.8 naming coverage.

title: A referred Echinerpeton neural spine
titleZh: Echinerpeton 归入标本的神经棘
regions: Sydney Mines Formation, Florence, Nova Scotia, Canada
summary: ROM VP 83326 records a hyper-elongated neural spine in a referred early synapsid specimen, while its whole-body outline and biological function remain unresolved.

evidenceItems.statement: ROM VP 83326 was referred to Echinerpeton intermedium after direct comparison with paratype RM 10057 and type-series casts and photographs; its preserved spine is at least 7 cm tall and about 2.3 mm wide.

uncertaintyItems.statement: The 308.5–305.5 Ma display interval is the paper's approximate Sydney Mines Formation envelope, not a direct radiometric date on ROM VP 83326 or a global Synapsida first appearance.

Because the centrum and most of the skeleton are absent, the reconstructed spine-to-centrum ratio and proposed display, recognition or thermoregulatory roles are estimates and hypotheses, not observed function or evidence of a direct mammalian ancestor.

title: Raranimus in a basal-therapsid matrix
titleZh: Raranimus 在基干兽孔类矩阵中的位置
regions: Dashankou locality, Xidagou Formation, Gansu, China
summary: Holotype IVPP V15424 supplies a fragmentary snout and a 71-character analysis that recovered Raranimus as sister to the other sampled therapsids.

evidenceItems.statement: IVPP V15424 is a roughly 100 mm partial, slightly crushed snout with a combination of cranial and dental characters; four shortest PAUP trees from the published 71-character matrix placed Raranimus immediately outside the remaining sampled Therapsida.

uncertaintyItems.statement: The recovered sister position belongs to one morphology matrix and its taxon-character sampling; it is not direct observation of ancestry, and the paper's Laurasian-origin interpretation remains a biogeographic hypothesis.

The 274.4–264.28 Ma display envelope is a broad current Middle Permian stage translation; the source explicitly reports no reliable radiometric dates for the Dashankou sequence, so it cannot establish a precise therapsid first appearance.

title: Haramiyavia and a matrix-defined crown boundary
titleZh: Haramiyavia 与矩阵限定的冠群边界
regions: Tait Bjerg Beds, Fleming Fjord Formation, East Greenland
summary: CT and dental-wear evidence from named Haramiyavia specimens informed a phylogenetic rescoring that placed Late Triassic haramiyids outside crown Mammalia in this study.

evidenceItems.statement: CT scans and three-dimensional occlusal reconstruction of mandibles MCZ7/95A–B and maxilla MCZ10/G95 documented the dentary condyle, postdentary trough and tooth-wear geometry used in the study's MorphoBank Project 2292 character matrix.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Results; Materials and Methods; SI Materials and Methods

uncertaintyItems.statement: The postdentary trough supports a mandibular-middle-ear interpretation, but the auditory ossicles are not preserved in articulation; the event therefore separates observed jaw anatomy from an ear-function inference.

Placement outside crown Mammalia is a result of the published matrix and rescoring, not an intrinsic label carried by the fossil or a universal calibration; competing haramiyidan placements require explicit alternative analyses.

title: Riograndia and Brasilodon break a jaw-joint ladder
titleZh: Riograndia 与 Brasilodon 打破颌关节阶梯叙事
regions: Riograndia Assemblage Zone, Candelária Sequence, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
summary: A 26-specimen μCT sample found a dentary–squamosal contact in Riograndia but not Brasilodon, supporting iterative acquisition rather than a single ancestor-to-descendant jaw-joint ladder.

evidenceItems.statement: μCT reconstructions of Riograndia specimens MPDC-1B1, UFRGS-PV-596-T, UFRGS-PV-833-T and UFRGS-PV-1319-T show dentary–squamosal contact, whereas the nine-specimen Brasilodon sample, including UFRGS-PV-929-T, -1030-T and -1043-T, lacks that articulation.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Cranial anatomy of Brasilodon; Cranial anatomy of Riograndia; Evolution of the mammalian jaw joint
Dataset record; segmented models, videos and phylogenetic matrices

uncertaintyItems.statement: Contact in Riograndia does not have the full condyle–glenoid morphology of the mammaliaform joint and does not confer crown-mammal membership; proposed bracing or synovial function remains an anatomical inference.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Cranial anatomy of Riograndia; Evolution of the mammalian jaw joint

uncertaintyItems.statement: 225.42 ± 0.37 Ma is reported as a maximum depositional age for the fossil-bearing assemblage, not a direct date on any skull; the displayed younger boundary is a broad Norian navigation limit and not a fossil LAD.

title: Dianoconodon and Feredocodon jaw–ear mosaics
titleZh: Dianoconodon 与 Feredocodon 的颌—耳镶嵌形态
regions: Lufeng Formation, Yunnan, and Daohugou Beds, Inner Mongolia, China
summary: Dianoconodon and Feredocodon preserve different jaw-joint and postdentary combinations that support a comparative reduction in load-bearing before complete middle-ear detachment.

evidenceItems.statement: Dianoconodon holotype IVPP V4257 and Feredocodon paratype IMMNH-PV01925 preserve articular, quadrate, dentary and postdentary anatomy used in MorphoBank Project 5075 and the archived phylogenetic analyses to compare jaw–ear configurations.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Cranial morphology; Jaw joint and middle ear; Methods

uncertaintyItems.statement: Reduced load-bearing and improved auditory suitability are inferred from morphology and finite comparative anatomy rather than directly measured hearing or bite forces in the fossils.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Jaw joint and middle ear; Discussion

uncertaintyItems.statement: The 201.4–161.5 Ma event range is a composite envelope spanning two fossils from separate formations and times; it is not one population, a continuous sequence, a direct ancestor–descendant pair or a crown-Mammalia origin interval.

title: Liaoconodon retains an ossified Meckelian link
titleZh: Liaoconodon 保留骨化麦氏软骨连接
summary: Holotype IVPP V16051 preserves detached ectotympanic and malleus elements still linked to the dentary by ossified Meckel's cartilage.

evidenceItems.statement: The near-complete articulated holotype IVPP V16051 preserves the ectotympanic and malleus without direct dentary attachment but connected to the dentary through an ossified Meckel's cartilage.

uncertaintyItems.statement: A proposed stabilizing role for the ossified Meckelian cartilage is a functional hypothesis from one fossil configuration; it does not make Liaoconodon a universal stage or a direct ancestor of living mammals.
The Aptian display envelope is a navigation translation of the formation-level Early Cretaceous occurrence, not a direct date on IVPP V16051 or evidence that all mammalian middle ears detached then.

title: Living experiments on Meckel's cartilage breakdown
titleZh: 现生实验检验麦氏软骨降解
regions: Laboratory mouse and gray short-tailed opossum developmental series
summary: Mouse genetic perturbation and opossum clast-cell inhibition test how Meckel's cartilage removal can uncouple the lower jaw from middle-ear elements during development.

evidenceItems.statement: c-Fos mutant mice retained and ossified Meckel's cartilage, while pharmacological inhibition of clast cells in Monodelphis domestica likewise delayed cartilage breakdown and produced a persistent jaw–ear connection phenotype.

uncertaintyItems.statement: These are present-day developmental perturbations in two living mammals: phenotype similarity does not mean ontogeny literally repeats the fossil record or prove that the same cellular mechanism produced any particular fossil jaw–ear condition.
The study identifies a role for clast cells but notes additional remodelling mechanisms and unresolved recruitment signals, so the mechanism is not treated as complete or universal across Mammalia.

title: Cartorhynchus holotype body-plan mosaic
titleZh: Cartorhynchus 正模体型镶嵌
regions: Upper member of the Nanlinghu Formation, Chaohu, Anhui, China
summary: The holotype preserves a short-snouted, short-trunked ichthyosauromorph with large flippers and dense limb bones; amphibious habits and suction feeding are bounded functional interpretations.

evidenceItems.statement: Holotype AGM I-1 preserves an articulated approximately 40-centimetre skeleton with a short rostrum, robust trunk, large flippers and thick cortical bone in the ribs and limbs.

uncertaintyItems.statement: A partly terrestrial lifestyle and suction feeding are anatomical and phylogenetic inferences, not behaviours directly observed in the fossil.

The published corrigendum corrected character descriptions and tree statistics without changing the reported topology; the specimen is not demonstrated to be a direct ancestor or a global first occurrence.

title: Chaohusaurus maternal specimen and embryos
titleZh: 巢湖鱼龙母体标本与胚胎
regions: Majiashan Quarry, Chaohu, Anhui, China; Procolumbites Zone
summary: Maternal specimen AGM I-1 preserves embryonic and neonatal remains associated with the body, directly documenting pregnancy in an Early Triassic ichthyosauromorph.

evidenceItems.statement: AGM I-1 contains a maternal skeleton, two embryos within the body and a neonate adjacent to the pelvis; one embryo is positioned head-first in the pelvic region.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Maternal specimen AGM I-1; Embryonic identification

uncertaintyItems.statement: Head-first delivery and a terrestrial origin of viviparity are comparative interpretations of orientation and topology rather than behaviours or ancestral states directly observed in AGM I-1.

title: Stenopterygius skin and blubber
titleZh: 狭翼鱼龙皮肤与脂肪层
summary: Chemical and microscopic analyses of specimen MH 432 resolve skin layers, blubber-like tissue and eumelanin-bearing structures in a Toarcian ichthyosaur.

evidenceItems.statement: MH 432 preserves scaleless skin with epidermal and dermal layers, a subcutaneous adipose layer interpreted as blubber, and eumelanin-bearing melanophores.

uncertaintyItems.statement: Countershading, thermoregulation and metabolic implications are interpretations built from tissue distribution and living analogues; they are not directly observed physiology or universal conditions for all ichthyosaurs.

title: Rhaeticosaurus holotype and bone histology
titleZh: Rhaeticosaurus 正模与骨组织学
regions: Exter Formation, Bonenburg, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
summary: Holotype LWL-MFN P 64047 provides an articulated Rhaetian plesiosaur skeleton and sampled long-bone histology, while its phylogenetic placement and physiology remain analytical inferences.

evidenceItems.statement: LWL-MFN P 64047 preserves a partial articulated skeleton from Rhaetian strata; humeral and femoral sections record rapidly deposited, highly vascularized bone tissue.

uncertaintyItems.statement: Recovery near the base of Pliosauridae is topology-dependent, and fast growth or elevated metabolism are histological interpretations rather than directly measured physiology.

title: Gravid Polycotylus specimen
titleZh: 怀孕多椎龙标本
summary: Adult specimen LACM 129639 contains a large conspecific fetus, directly supporting viviparity in this Late Cretaceous plesiosaur.

evidenceItems.statement: LACM 129639 preserves an adult Polycotylus latipinnus with a single articulated fetus inside the body cavity; shared diagnostic characters support conspecific identification.

referenceLinks.figure: Figures 1–3; Supporting Online Material Figure S1
referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Description; Identification of the embryonic individual

uncertaintyItems.statement: A K-selected strategy, sociality and parental care are life-history inferences from offspring size and living analogues, not behaviours preserved in this specimen.

title: Four-flipper plesiosaur hydrodynamic experiment
titleZh: 蛇颈龙四鳍水动力实验
summary: A physical flipper model tested phase relationships and measured thrust, torque and efficiency; it constrains plausible swimming mechanics rather than observing an extinct gait.

evidenceItems.statement: Water-channel trials of paired fore- and hind-flipper models found that certain phase offsets increased hind-flipper thrust and whole-system efficiency through vortex interaction.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Methods; Results: effect of phase on thrust and efficiency

uncertaintyItems.statement: The apparatus used reconstructed rigid flippers and prescribed kinematics; its measured performance does not prove one universal stroke for every plesiosaur taxon, speed or manoeuvre.

title: Tupandactylus feathers and melanosomes
titleZh: 古神翼龙羽状结构与黑素体
summary: Specimen MCT.R.1884 preserves cranial soft tissues, monofilaments and branched feather-like structures with distinct melanosome geometries.

evidenceItems.statement: MCT.R.1884, preserved across five slabs, includes a partial skull and crest with monofilaments, branched feather-like structures and melanosomes in skin and filament samples.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Specimen description; Feather morphology; Melanosome geometry

uncertaintyItems.statement: Colour signalling and the ancestral state of feathers are evolutionary interpretations; the study does not directly recover exact colours or establish that every pterosaur bore the same structures.

title: Hamipterus egg and embryo assemblage
titleZh: 哈密翼龙卵与胚胎聚集体
regions: Shengjinkou Formation, Turpan-Hami Basin, Xinjiang, China
summary: A Lower Cretaceous accumulation exposes 215 eggs in one block, with hundreds inferred and 16 eggs containing embryonic remains across multiple horizons.

evidenceItems.statement: A 3.28-square-metre sandstone block exposes 215 Hamipterus eggs, possibly about 300 in the block, and the broader sample includes 16 eggs with embryonic bones across at least four stratigraphic levels.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Egg accumulation; Embryonic remains; Geological context

uncertaintyItems.statement: Storm transport, colonial nesting and site fidelity are taphonomic or behavioural interpretations; hatchling flightlessness and parental care depend on embryonic stage and ossification assumptions and are not treated here as direct observations.

title: Giant-pterosaur flight and launch model
titleZh: 巨型翼龙飞行与起飞模型
summary: Comparative scaling, bone mechanics and aerodynamic calculations test flight and quadrupedal-launch feasibility for giant pterosaur reconstructions.

evidenceItems.statement: Model calculations using reconstructed mass, wing planform, bone strength and non-avian launch kinematics found powered flight and quadrupedal launch mechanically feasible for the sampled giant pterosaur reconstructions.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Flap-gliding analysis; Flight performance; Launch mechanisms

uncertaintyItems.statement: The result is a biomechanical feasibility argument, not an observed launch, a universal gait for all pterosaurs or a direct measurement of extinct body mass and muscle power.

title: Indohyus skull, bone-density and isotope sample
titleZh: 印多霍斯兽头骨、骨密度与同位素样本
regions: Sindkhatudi bone bed, Upper Subathu Group, Kalakot, Jammu and Kashmir, India
summary: Separately catalogued skulls, limb bones and teeth support an aquatic-wading interpretation and a raoellid sister placement to Cetacea in the published analysis.

evidenceItems.statement: Skulls RR 207 and RR 208 preserve the cetacean-like involucrum; RR 157 and RR 42 provide dense long-bone sections, and a multi-tooth stable-isotope sample differs from terrestrial artiodactyl comparators.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Osteology; Bone histology; Stable-isotope analysis; Phylogeny

uncertaintyItems.statement: The material is a disarticulated bone-bed sample, not one associated skeleton; aquatic wading and sister-group position are inferences, and Indohyus is neither crown Cetacea nor demonstrated to be a direct ancestor.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Specimen descriptions; Phylogenetic and ecological discussion

title: Pakicetus locality-composite terrestrial skeleton
titleZh: 巴基鲸地点组合的陆生骨架
regions: H-GSP Locality 62, Ganda Kas, Kala Chitta Hills, Punjab, Pakistan
summary: A locality-composite Pakicetus reconstruction records weight-bearing limbs and a terrestrial locomotor body plan while retaining diagnostic early-cetacean cranial anatomy.

evidenceItems.statement: Skull H-GSP 96231 and separately catalogued vertebrae and limb elements, including humerus H-GSP 92042 and calcaneum H-GSP 96420, form the published Pakicetus reconstruction and support terrestrial locomotion.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Postcranial osteology; Skeleton reconstruction; Hearing and locomotion discussion

uncertaintyItems.statement: The reconstruction combines multiple individuals and the 2001 morphological tree did not recover Hippopotamidae as the immediate cetacean sister group; neither result overrides later independent retroposon topology.

title: Ambulocetus holotype locomotor mosaic
titleZh: 陆行鲸正模的运动镶嵌
regions: Kuldana Formation, Kala Chitta Hills, Punjab, Pakistan
summary: Partial skeleton H-GSP 18507 combines large weight-bearing limbs with a vertebral and hind-limb morphology used to model amphibious swimming.

evidenceItems.statement: Holotype H-GSP 18507 preserves a partial skull, vertebral column and substantial fore- and hind-limb material from the Kuldana Formation, directly documenting an amphibious anatomical mosaic.

uncertaintyItems.statement: Otter-like dorsoventral swimming and sea-lion-like movement on land are functional models derived from anatomy and living analogues, not observed behaviour; the holotype is not a direct ancestor.

title: Peregocetus holotype and South Pacific occurrence
titleZh: 游走鲸正模与南太平洋出现记录
regions: Lowest Yumaque Member, Paracas Formation, Playa Media Luna, Pisco Basin, Peru
summary: Holotype MUSM 3580 anchors a 42.6 Ma protocetid occurrence in Peru and preserves a sacral attachment, robust limbs and hoof-like terminal phalanges.

evidenceItems.statement: MUSM 3580 preserves mandibles and most major postcranial regions; two fused sacrals, a defined femoral head and hoof-like distal phalanges support weight-bearing capability alongside aquatic adaptations.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Locality and horizon; Diagnosis; Postcranial description; STAR Methods

uncertaintyItems.statement: The paper calls Protocetidae paraphyletic; walking, swimming and the favoured westward South Atlantic route are reconstructions, while an eastward route and the presence of a tail fluke remain unresolved.

title: Basilosaurus reduced hind-limb specimens
titleZh: 龙王鲸退化后肢标本
regions: Birket Qarun Formation, Wadi Al Hitan, Fayum, Egypt
summary: Egyptian Basilosaurus specimens preserve a tiny jointed pelvic limb and foot, while a named femur supplies measured bone-microstructure evidence.

evidenceItems.statement: The original Egyptian material preserves an innominate and articulated limb-and-foot elements; separately, male specimen UM 93231 contributes an explicitly catalogued femur with measured compact bone microstructure.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Pelvis, hind limb and foot description; Functional discussion

uncertaintyItems.statement: The small limb was not weight-bearing and does not imply terrestrial locomotion; its proposed use as a copulatory guide and organism-wide swimming consequences are functional interpretations, not directly observed behaviour.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Discussion of basilosaurid bone microstructure and locomotion

title: Aegicetus holotype and tail-driven transition model
titleZh: 盾鲸正模与尾驱动过渡模型
regions: Lower Gehannam Formation, WH-203, Wadi Al Hitan, Fayum, Egypt

evidenceItems.statement: The described sample includes a stem coleopterid, a holometabolous larva, a stem hymenopterid, an early hemipteran and an early psocodean.

uncertaintyItems.statement: The specimens do not demonstrate synchronous origins, exact crown-order first appearances or a single climatic cause for later diversification.

title: Vegavis skull tests a Cretaceous crown-bird hypothesis
titleZh: Vegavis 头骨检验白垩纪冠群鸟假说
summary: A nearly complete Antarctic skull supplies direct anatomy and a new combined topology, while older conflicting placements remain visible.

evidenceItems.statement: AMNH FARB 30899 preserves a toothless beak, crown-like neuroanatomy and specialized jaw apparatus

uncertaintyItems.statement: Published analyses have recovered stem-anatid, stem-anseriform and outside-Aves alternatives

title: Mosasauroidea is broader than Mosasauridae
titleZh: 沧龙超科范围大于沧龙科
regions: Cretaceous mosasauroid records; middle Turonian of north-central Texas
summary: Explicit phylogenetic definitions separate broad Mosasauroidea from node-defined Mosasauridae, while Dallasaurus shows that family placement need not imply fully paddle-like limbs.

evidenceItems.statement: Table 1 defines Mosasauroidea and Mosasauridae separately; the Dallasaurus skeletons preserve plesiopedal limbs in a taxon recovered within Mosasauridae by the original analysis.

uncertaintyItems.statement: Basal mosasauroid relationships and some traditional names are sensitive to analytical strategy; the navigation edge therefore supports discovery and does not assert a single immutable taxonomy.

title: Bobosaurus as an older uncertain plesiosaur-line candidate
titleZh: 更老但不确定的近蛇颈龙候选 Bobosaurus
regions: Rio del Lago Formation, northeastern Italy
summary: The early Carnian holotype combines nothosaurian and plesiosaurian features, but its position remains an alternative-sensitive hypothesis and is not used to extend diagnostic Plesiosauria.

evidenceItems.statement: Holotype MFSN 27285 preserves an articulated sauropterygian skeleton from the lower Carnian Rio del Lago Formation with a documented mosaic of nothosaurian and plesiosaurian characters.

uncertaintyItems.statement: The original study considered a pistosaurid position or a closer relationship to Plesiosauria; this older candidate is displayed beside, not substituted for, diagnostic Rhaetian Rhaeticosaurus.

title: Maghriboselache documents a broad-snouted Devonian symmoriiform
titleZh: Maghriboselache 记录泥盆纪宽吻对称鳍鲨形软骨鱼
regions: Thylacocephalan Layer, southern Maïder and Tafilalt, eastern Anti-Atlas, Morocco
summary: Several partly articulated Famennian specimens preserve three-dimensional neurocrania, a broad cartilage-enclosed snout, widely separated nasal capsules, a high-aspect-ratio tail and large pectoral fins; the sample records sensory and body-plan disparity without dating a global crown origin.

evidenceItems.statement: The holotype AA.MEM.DS.12 and referred specimen PIMUZ A/I 5159 preserve three-dimensional cranial anatomy, while the Thylacocephalan Layer sample also preserves partly articulated body and fin anatomy.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Introduction; Material; Systematic palaeontology; neurocranium description

evidenceItems.statement: In PIMUZ A/I 5155, the stomach contains a more or less articulated small actinopterygian approximately 40 mm long, recording one feeding event.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Description—Soft tissues; paragraph beginning ‘Consequently, the body outline is discernible...’

evidenceItems.statement: The broad rostrum and laterally separated nasal capsules are described as an early sensory specialization, while the time-calibrated placement remains matrix-dependent.

uncertaintyItems.statement: Most skeletons have missing caudal regions and some cranial parts are compressed; body length, sex and ecology therefore remain sample-bounded interpretations.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Material and methods; body form and preservation

uncertaintyItems.statement: The event is a Moroccan specimen record and does not establish direct ancestry, a global FAD/LAD or an uninterrupted holocephalan lineage.

title: Strudiella insect diagnosis and re-assessment
titleZh: Strudiella 昆虫诊断与再评估
summary: A Late Devonian specimen was first described as a complete insect and later re-examined as an arthropod that cannot be securely identified as an insect.

evidenceItems.statement: Garrouste et al. named and interpreted the nearly complete Strud specimen as Strudiella devonica, a terrestrial Late Devonian insect.

uncertaintyItems.statement: Hörnschemeyer et al. rejected the insect identification after re-investigation; the atlas preserves this disagreement rather than using Strudiella as a secure insect calibration.

title: Cosmoselachus reveals an operculate symmoriiform
titleZh: Cosmoselachus 揭示具鳃盖的对称鳍鲨形软骨鱼
regions: Fayetteville Shale near Cove Creek, Searcy County, Arkansas, United States
summary: CT reconstruction of the partial holotype AMNH FF 20509 documents elongate fused branchial rays forming a corrugated operculate structure over posterior gill arches, adding a bounded Carboniferous body-plan sample to the early chondrichthyan record.

evidenceItems.statement: AMNH FF 20509 preserves lower jaws with teeth, a partial upper jaw and basicranium, branchial elements, pectoral cartilage and fin material from the Fayetteville Shale.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Abstract; Material; Systematic palaeontology; specimen description

evidenceItems.statement: The study identifies elongate rays extending from the hyoid and branchial arches and fused into an operculum covering at least two posterior branchial arches.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: CT reconstruction; branchial anatomy; phylogenetic analysis

uncertaintyItems.statement: The holotype is partial and has experienced damage and pyrite decay; body size, complete locomotion and population variation are unavailable.
The phylogenetic placement is a sampled analysis and the event is not a global symmoriiform or Chondrichthyes endpoint, direct ancestor or complete species range.

title: Cretophasmomima wing pattern and proposed leaf crypsis
titleZh: Cretophasmomima 翅脉图案与拟叶隐蔽假说
regions: Yixian Formation, Jehol biota, Inner Mongolia, China
summary: The Early Cretaceous stick-insect fossil preserves dark wing veins that the describing study compared with a contemporaneous leaf-shaped plant organ as a possible crypsis model.

evidenceItems.statement: The primary description documents the wing pattern and its comparison with Membranifolia admirabilis in the Jehol setting.

referenceLinks.quoteLocator: Wing coloration, plant comparison and proposed crypsis

uncertaintyItems.statement: The fossil preserves a pattern and a proposed model, not observed predator avoidance, feeding behaviour or measured crypsis performance.
